title: An AI-racing drone beat the best humans and set a world record
key_facts: A Delft University of Technology (Netherlands) team built MonoRace, a lightweight AI-piloted racing drone.
It won first place at the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League in November 2025, beating all other AI teams and three former human world champion pilots.
It reached roughly 62 mph; the team says this is the first AI-piloted drone to beat human pilots in an international racing competition.
A University of Zurich AI drone (Swift) beat human racers in 2022, but only on an indoor track built for it.
MonoRace runs on a small onboard computer using a camera and an inertial measurement unit, issuing an estimated 500 commands per second.
A neural network trained by reinforcement learning in simulation controls the motors directly.
New details were published on 14 Oct 2026 in the journal Science Robotics.
quote_evidence: The team won this race in November 2025 but new details about the science behind this achievement are published today in the journal Science Robotics.
During its flights, MonoRace topped speeds of roughly 62 miles per hour as it looped, dove, and zipped through gates.

According to the team, these results make MonoRace the first AI-piloted drone to beat human pilots in an international racing competition, and could have an impact on drone racing and physical AI more broadly.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI that flies fast with little sensing hardware points to machines that can move safely in the real world.
notes: Race result is older (Nov 2025); the new item is the peer-reviewed paper. 'First' is the team's claim.
